issues.description: Two parallel config registries (MODEL_CONFIGS for STT, TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS) duplicate the same dispatch pattern across files without sharing it.
issues.detail: Both modules invent the same shape: a frozen dataclass plus a string-keyed dict plus capability flags plus a default. That is the right move (data over conditionals), but it is now two implementations of one idea, and any future model will tempt a third. Lift the pattern to one tiny module so the shape is named once.

issues.description: Capability booleans complect three orthogonal facts: what the API accepts, what the SDK method is, and what the default value is.
issues.detail: ModelConfig mixes supports_prompt/supports_mode/supports_language with default_language/default_mode and with use_translate_endpoint/use_translate_method. Validation, dispatch, and defaulting are three concerns braided into one record. Splitting them (a capability set, a dispatch tag, a defaults map) would let each be reasoned about and tested independently.

issues.description: get_speakers_for_model silently falls back to v2 speakers for unknown models, hiding a fact behind a default.
issues.detail: Returning v2 speakers for an unknown model name is a place-oriented convenience that erases the distinction between "this model exists and has speakers" and "we have no idea what this is." Callers cannot tell which case they are in. Return an empty list or raise; do not invent data.

issues.description: Automatic pace clamping for v3 silently rewrites caller-supplied values instead of surfacing the fact.
issues.detail: The PR description advertises "automatic parameter clamping for pace when outside v3 range." Clamping is a value transformation that the caller did not ask for; it confuses what the caller said with what the system did. Validate and reject, or log loudly and pass through, but do not quietly mutate the input.

issues.description: Enums of speaker names duplicate the same data already encoded in the config dict's speakers tuple.
issues.detail: SarvamTTSSpeakerV2 and SarvamTTSSpeakerV3 are values masquerading as types. The tuple in TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS is already the source of truth and is built from the enum, so the enum is paying for type-safety it does not actually enforce at the API boundary. One of the two should go; the data is enough.

issues.description: Default speaker for v3 disagrees between the dataclass docstring (aditya) and the config value (shubh).
issues.detail: TTSModelConfig docstring and the PR description say v3 default is aditya; TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS sets default_speaker="shubh". Two sources of truth for one fact, already drifting before merge. Pick one, delete the other, and let the data answer the question.

review.summary: The refactor moves both services from string-sniffing if/else chains ("saaras" in model.lower()) to data-driven config tables, which is the right direction: dispatch becomes a value, not control flow. The remaining issues are about how far the decomposition went. Capability flags, dispatch tags, and defaults are still complected inside one dataclass; two near-identical config registries live in two files; and a few places (speaker fallback, pace clamping, dual speaker sources) quietly substitute defaults for facts the caller supplied. Decision: COMPLECTED on the config shape, SIMPLE on the dispatch direction. The question that should have been asked first: what is the smallest set of facts that distinguish one Sarvam model from another, and where does that table live?
